definition: Engaging customers or clients to reduce product-use, transport or other value-chain greenhouse gas emissions.
Engaging portfolio companies, borrowers or investees on transition plans, climate targets and financed emissions.
Contractual or purchasing requirements that suppliers set climate targets, disclose emissions or satisfy climate-related standards.
Auditing, assessing or monitoring supplier compliance with climate requirements or greenhouse gas performance.
Supplier training, workshops, technical assistance or capability building to measure and reduce emissions.
Joint emissions-reduction projects and innovation with suppliers, customers or other value-chain partners.
Requesting supplier emissions inventories, product carbon footprints or climate disclosures and using these data in purchasing or Scope 3 accounting.
Corrective action, remediation, escalation or termination in response to suppliers failing environmental or climate requirements.
Prioritizing stakeholder engagement based on emissions, procurement spending, risk, influence or supply-chain coverage.
Engaging smallholder farmers on agricultural practices, deforestation, land use or greenhouse gas reduction.
Protecting operations and infrastructure against floods, heat, storms or other physical climate hazards through adaptation measures.
Business continuity, emergency planning, redundant supply or operational resilience measures for climate-related disruptions.
Insurance, hedging or other financial risk-transfer arrangements addressing climate-related losses.
Water conservation, reuse, alternative water sourcing or water-management measures addressing climate-related scarcity.
Using climate scenarios or stress tests to assess exposure, prioritize responses or inform transition planning.
